task_completion.description: Open the Fetchers configuration dialog via the Tools menu.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A dialog window titled 'Fetchers' is visible over the main Angry IP Scanner window.

task_completion.description: Select 'Web Detect' from the Available fetchers list.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The item 'Web Detect' is highlighted or selected in the right-hand list of the Fetchers dialog.

task_completion.description: Move 'Web Detect' to the Selected fetchers list.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The item 'Web Detect' appears in the left-hand 'Selected fetchers' list.

task_completion.description: Move 'MAC Vendor' to the Selected fetchers list.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The item 'MAC Vendor' appears in the left-hand 'Selected fetchers' list alongside the default fetchers.

task_completion.description: Click OK to save the fetcher configuration.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The Fetchers dialog window closes, returning focus to the main application window.

task_completion.description: Verify the main scan results table displays the new columns.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The main table header now shows six columns in total, specifically including 'Web Detect' and 'MAC Vendor' as the last two columns.

integrity.description: The agent used the graphical user interface rather than command line arguments.
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots show the mouse cursor interacting with the 'Tools' menu and the 'Fetchers' dialog buttons.

integrity.description: The agent interacted with the real Angry IP Scanner application.
integrity.visual_evidence: The window decorations, icons, and specific 'Fetchers' dialog layout match the Java-based Angry IP Scanner interface.

integrity.description: The agent did not bypass the UI by editing configuration files in a text editor.
integrity.visual_evidence: No text editors (like leafpad or nano) are seen being used to modify internal application settings.

privileged_info_for_vlm: The default fetchers in Angry IP Scanner are IP, Ping, Hostname, and Ports. The '<' button is the specific button used to move items from the right (Available) to the left (Selected) list. The final state must show 'Web Detect' and 'MAC Vendor' as visible column headers in the main results table.
